name: Install CLI and Create Standard Profiles
query: I want to start using Conductor but I don't have anything set up yet
expected_behavior: Step 2: If missing, prefer `npx @conductor-oss/conductor-cli` for one-off use. Ask before any global npm install; if npm is unavailable, explain the Node.js prerequisite or fallback limitations.
Step 3: Start the standard dual-profile onboarding rather than asking the user to choose only one server.
Step 4: Open https://developer.orkescloud.com/ visibly when browser automation is available, let the user sign in, and use visible navigation to Access Control → Applications.
Step 5: Guide the user to create a least-privilege application and hand control to them before Create access key. Never observe the one-time secret or request credentials in chat.
Step 6: Have the user run interactive `conductor config save --profile developer` and directly enter `https://developer.orkescloud.com/api`, Enterprise, and their API key + secret.
Step 7: Have the user run interactive `conductor config save --profile localhost` with `http://localhost:8080/api`, OSS, and no auth. Saving it does not require starting the server.
Step 8: Verify with `conductor config list`, `conductor --profile developer whoami`, and `conductor --profile developer workflow list --json`; verify localhost only when its server is running.
Step 9: Default later skill commands to `--profile developer`; use `--profile localhost` when the user asks for local.
success_criteria: CLI presence is checked before installation
One-off npx is preferred and global npm installation requires explicit consent
Both `developer` and `localhost` profiles are created for an unqualified first-time setup
Developer Edition browser navigation is visible and access-key creation is handed off to the user
Credential values never enter chat, agent tool input, command arguments, clipboard reads, or raw-profile inspection
The localhost profile is saved without unnecessarily starting a server
Developer profile verification uses a real authenticated API call
